title: The Fire Lab
story: A fire drill has locked you and NOVA in the science lab. NOVA must understand burning and how to control it before the doors will open. Careful: wrong fire advice is dangerous.
escaped: The doors unlock. NOVA now knows what burns, how to put out different fires and what a flame's zones are.

locks.title: Will it burn?
locks.intro: NOVA must sort materials into combustible (burn in air, giving heat and light) and non-combustible. Choose its clues.

features.text: Burns in air giving heat and light

locks.hint: A matchstick and a steel spoon are both solids found in the kitchen. What is different about them?
locks.learn: Clues like 'solid' or 'in the kitchen' were true for both groups, so they confused NOVA. The defining property, burning in air, sorts every case.

locks.title: Check NOVA's fire advice
locks.intro: NOVA is helping write a fire safety poster. Is this line right? Decide and pick the fact that settles it.
locks.claim: Pour water on any fire, even an electrical fire or burning petrol, to put it out fast.
evidence: Water is not suitable for fires in electrical equipment or burning oil and petrol; carbon dioxide is the best extinguisher for these.
Water cools a burning substance below its ignition temperature.
A candle flame has three zones.
LPG has a high calorific value.
locks.hint: Water does put out many fires. Is that true for ALL fires?
locks.learn: AI answers often over-generalise: true for wood fires, dangerous for electrical and oil fires. The word 'any' is a signal to check the exceptions.

locks.title: Why did the candles go out?
locks.intro: Three lit candles: one in the open, one under a small glass jar and one under a big glass jar.
locks.question: NOVA says: 'Glass jars put out flames because glass is cold.' What is the honest explanation?
options: NOVA is right: cold glass cools the flame.
The candle uses up the air (oxygen) in the jar; a bigger jar holds more air, so the candle burns longer.
locks.hint: Both jars were glass. What else is different between the small jar and the big jar?
locks.learn: When NOVA picked a cause, it ignored a detail in the data: jar size changed how long the candle burned. A good explanation fits all the data: combustion needs air.

locks.title: Fix NOVA's flame map
locks.intro: NOVA has labelled the zones of a candle flame. Tick the labels that are wrong.

rows.label: Hottest part of the flame
rows.why: the innermost zone is the least hot: unburnt wax vapour

rows.label: Uses the outermost zone to melt gold
Sooty, incomplete combustion
rows.why: the blue outer zone burns completely and is the hottest

locks.hint: Which zone do goldsmiths use, and why?
locks.learn: Two wrong labels flip the facts about heat. A model trained on them would give exactly the wrong answer when it matters, so check the examples that disagree with each other.
